# AI access

Let Claude or another AI tool read and act here through MCP, as one person, with that person’s rights.

Module id `ai-access`, in [src/modules/ai-access/](../../../src/modules/ai-access/module.json).

## Requirements

- `MCP-TOKENS`: An admin can make a personal token for any person, named for what it is for; it is shown once, only its SHA-256 hash is stored, and it can be revoked. An AI assistant using it through the MCP server acts as that person: the same rights and rules as the app, every change logged as theirs via MCP, writes checkable with a dry run, and a revoked or wrong token refused. (Replace by R1.)
- `TOKENS-SERVER-ONLY`: AI assistant tokens are made and revoked only by security-definer functions (okr_token_create, okr_token_revoke) that make the secret in the database, store only its SHA-256 hash and return it once. The public key can't read, add or change okr_api_tokens; the app lists token metadata (never the hash) with okr_token_list, and the MCP server finds a token with okr_token_find. The public key can't read okr_feedback; Workspace reads a workspace's with okr_feedback_list. AI assistants and Workspace's feedback keep working. (Replace by R1.)
- `AI-ACCESS-OPTIONAL`: An admin switches AI access off for a workspace. Off, the MCP server refuses every token of the workspace with one sentence that says so (it still lists its tools, and a refused request doesn’t count as a token’s use), no token can be made, and Workspace, Settings and People show no tokens; a token can still be revoked. Switching it off first names the tokens that stop working, and switching it back on names those that work again. Tokens are kept, not revoked. (Copy.) Tests: `evals/mcp.eval.ts`.
